A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same full-parameter ES fine-tuning research. Their main text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Countdown accuracies, repeated-run conciseness experiments, learning curves, and parameter-magnitude analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original ES evaluations on math reasoning, Mini Sudoku, and ARC-AGI.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same perturbation, reward normalization, parameter update, greedy decoding, and memory-saving procedures. Algorithm 2 moves to Appendix A.1. The new disclosure about correlated noise from layerwise seed reuse describes the current implementation; it does not establish a version-to-version procedural change.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained Countdown and conciseness tasks, v2 adds MATH training and evaluation on AIME2024, Minerva Math, OlympiadBench, AMC, and MATH500. It also adds 4×4 Mini Sudoku and ARC-AGI, substantially broadening coverage to competition mathematics, constraint-solving puzzles, and grid-transformation reasoning.

E2.justification: The original Countdown PPO and GRPO comparisons remain as PPO-z and GRPO-z, while Table 1 adds evaluated VERL implementations GRPO-v and Dr.GRPO-v. The new math comparison evaluates SimpleRL-Zero (GRPO), OpenReasoner-Zero (PPO), and Oat-Zero (Dr.GRPO) checkpoints. The conciseness comparator remains GRPO.

E3.justification: New math experiments introduce Qwen2.5-Math-7B, difficulty-3–5 MATH training, a 3,000-token response limit, pass@1 evaluation, and checkpoint selection using evaluation scores, including MATH500 as pseudo-validation. New puzzle protocols specify training/test splits, populations, and iteration budgets; added VERL baselines introduce their own configurations. The previously stated Countdown and conciseness settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a preliminary correlated-noise versus independent-noise comparison, reporting similar performance without quantitative supporting results. Figure 11 adds a before/after Sudoku output case study, and the retained Countdown example's mismatched input is corrected. Existing conciseness sensitivity experiments and parameter-shift analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report four-seed conciseness experiments with means and standard deviations, including the extended learning-rate sweeps. v2 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure. Its three selected math checkpoints are not reported as independent repeated runs.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–2 entries remain, but v2 adds substantial Countdown, math, and puzzle results and corrects some Countdown improvement bars. For Qwen2.5-0.5B, newly evaluated GRPO-v and Dr.GRPO-v achieve 13.0% and 13.5%, alongside retained ES accuracy of 14.4%. Sudoku results conflict internally: Table 3 reports base/fine-tuned accuracies of 2.5%/69.5%, whereas Appendix A.8 reports 2%/66.5%.

T1.justification: The ES update equations, reward standardization, and KL approximation retain their mathematical content. Relocating the KL formula and detailed algorithm does not change the mathematics. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v2 adds none.

C1.justification: The first billion-scale full-parameter ES contribution remains, but v2 removes explicit sample-efficiency superiority from the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, together with the prominent small-model RL-failure argument. Its stated contributions now include competitiveness with strong math reasoning baselines and successful application to ARC-AGI and Sudoku, materially revising the empirical claim scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial interpretations concerning RL implementation complexity, ES communication and memory advantages, and future inference optimizations. It qualifies math comparisons because baseline training datasets differ. The new Impact Statement extrapolates reduced reward hacking to preservation of ethical guardrails and safer nonexpert fine-tuning, without corresponding new ethical evaluations.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the Countdown implementation libraries, discloses layerwise seed reuse, and explains the previously unexplained mapping of conciseness rewards to [0,1]. New appendices document math grading, prompts, checkpoint selection, and puzzle generation, splits, preprocessing, and hyperparameters. The source-code link remains available despite removal of the separate reproducibility statement.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around contemporary RL implementations and design choices, adding discussion and citations for Dr.GRPO, SimpleRL, OpenReasoner, OAT/VERL, clipping, and KL regularization, alongside math and puzzle research. Countdown attribution changes from Goodfellow et al. to Gandhi et al. (2024). The foundational ES background is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten, and related work and discussion gain topical organization. Algorithm 2 and task/metric explanations move into expanded appendices. New empirical subsections, an Impact Statement, and acknowledgments substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, expands Table 1 and the Countdown plots, and adds the math comparison figure, puzzle-results table, math prompt table, and Sudoku/ARC displays. Retained figures and tables are resized or relocated, and Algorithm 2 moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: Stronger Countdown comparators, corrected examples and plots, clearer implementation disclosures, and removal of prominent sample-efficiency claims make v2 more credible and reproducible. Broader experiments add useful evidence, but their contribution is limited by evaluation-based math checkpoint selection (Appendix A.6), conflicting Sudoku scores (Table 3 versus Appendix A.8), and unsupported ethical extrapolations. These tradeoffs support a limited net quality improvement.
